title: This government takes 35% of the economy in tax. Top 5 highest taxes
description: Which government collects the most tax compared to the size of its economy? Number one will surprise you. Real World Bank data (central government tax revenue, % of GDP, 2024), counted down from five to one.
source: World Bank, tax revenue (% of GDP, central government, 2024, 93 countries with 2024 data), data.worldbank.org/indicator/GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS

segments.text: One government collects taxes worth thirty-five percent of its whole economy. Can you guess which?

props.kicker: Tax revenue, share of the economy

segments.text: Top five. Number five is Luxembourg. Almost twenty-nine percent.
Number four is New Zealand. Almost thirty percent.
Number three is the one you expected. Denmark. Thirty-three percent.
Number two is home to the oldest desert on Earth. Namibia. Almost thirty-four percent.
And number one is Lesotho. Thirty-five percent. A customs union with South Africa hands it a big share of shared import duties.
And it's no fluke. Lesotho hit forty percent in 2009 and again in 2023.
The other extreme is the United Arab Emirates. Under one percent. Oil pays the bills.
This counts central government taxes only. Where does your country land? Follow for more money, mapped.
